subject.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors

question: Should LINE rapid follow-up events from the same stable sender be skipped with a busy reply by default, or should the channel preserve them through queueing or another delivery path?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes user-visible delivery semantics, and source tests cannot decide whether dropping a distinct second LINE message is the product behavior maintainers want.

options.title: Require proof, then accept busy-skip
options.body: Keep this PR shape if redacted real LINE proof demonstrates the busy reply, release behavior, and group isolation clearly enough for the default-on delivery tradeoff.

options.title: Preserve follow-up messages
options.body: Pause this PR and design a queue or active-turn feedback path that prevents lock contention without dropping the second user message.

options.title: Narrow the guard scope
options.body: Limit the guard to the smallest proven LINE surface, such as stable direct-message senders, until group and postback delivery semantics are explicitly accepted.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept busy-skip
recommendation.body: Keep this PR shape if redacted real LINE proof demonstrates the busy reply, release behavior, and group isolation clearly enough for the default-on delivery tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent sampled history on the touched LINE handler/context files and is the best available owner for the delivery-semantics choice.
